title: Block Generated File Edits
summary: A Claude Code hook that refuses edits to files whose first lines say they are generated, so the agent changes the source and not the output.
description: Generated files get overwritten the next time the generator runs, so any hand edit is lost work. This PreToolUse hook opens the target file before an Edit or Write and looks at its first ten lines for markers such as @generated, DO NOT EDIT or Code generated by.
When it finds one it stops the edit and tells the agent to change the generator input instead. New files and files without a marker pass straight through.
useWhen: Protect protobuf, GraphQL or OpenAPI output from hand edits
Keep an agent out of lockfile-style generated code
Force changes into the schema instead of the compiled result
Avoid diffs that vanish after the next codegen run

hook.command: node -e "process.on('uncaughtException',()=>process.exit(0));let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c).on('end',()=>{let j={};try{j=JSON.parse(d)||{}}catch(e){process.exit(0)}const i=j.tool_input||{};const f=String(i.file_path||'');const fs=require('fs');if(!f||!fs.existsSync(f))process.exit(0);let h='';try{h=fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8').slice(0,1500)}catch(e){process.exit(0)}const m=h.split('\n').slice(0,10).join('\n').match(/@generated|do not edit|auto-?generated|code generated|generated by|this file is generated/i);if(m){console.error('Blocked: '+f+' is marked as generated ('+m[0]+'). Change the source or the generator and regenerate it instead of editing the output.');process.exit(2)}process.exit(0)})"

example.prompt: Add a field to the User type in src/gen/user.pb.go.
example.result: The edit is blocked because the header says Code generated by protoc. The agent edits user.proto and runs the generator instead.

faq.question: How does it know a file is generated?
faq.answer: It reads the first ten lines and matches common header phrases like @generated, DO NOT EDIT and auto-generated, ignoring case.

faq.question: Will it stop me creating a brand new file?
faq.answer: No. A path that does not exist yet is skipped, so only existing marked files are protected.

access: Reads the first lines of the file about to be changed
Blocks the edit when a marker is found; changes nothing itself
